liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dark Star** (5 reviews, 1 other source): Reviewer ranks this Dark Star among the top three of all time; Recommends the Dark Star > Me and My Uncle > Dark Star > Wharf Rat > Sugar Magnolia sequence as strong [2][3][4][8][11][13]
- **Black Throated Wind** (1 review): Reviewer hears a transcendent Black Throated Wind [11]

## Setlist highlights

- **Stars & Stripes tuning**: mythic rare: 2 archived performances [15]

## The recordings

- **gd72-04-24.sbd-aud.cotsman.16332.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 27 songs; 201 min; rated 4.06/5 by 18 [1]. Said about its sound: The circulating copy is listenable but degraded compared with the soundboard release expected from the band; First set sounds weaker, with an audience-source feel; second set is better, a soundboard showing a generation or two of wear [3][4]
- **gd1972-04-24.aud.unknown.6956.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 26 songs; 191 min; rated 2.2/5 by 5 [2]. Said about its sound: This soundboard is fair: better than earlier versions, though other copies sound better and vocals are hard to hear; Audience portions are average at best; soundboard has noise, skips, a splice and speed flutter [2][12]

## Around the show

- Reviewer says Bobby and Pigpen are both in excellent voice [11]
- Calls it the highlight of Europe '72, though 5/10 could be argued instead [3]
- Official release sounds far better than earlier versions; reviewer places show among the top three of Europe '72 [7]
- Before the official release, only far inferior copies of the show circulated [8]
- Reviewer says every song here is the best version except Dark Star, which is not the best [9]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd72-04-24.sbd-aud.cotsman.16332.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Jeff Cotsman; source: Soundboard and Audience Composite [1]. Also: Official three-disc release Rockin' the Rhein was mixed from the original 16-track analog masters and mastered in HDCD; Source 2 runs soundboard through unknown steps to digital, CD, EAC and SHN via Jeff Cook and Chuck Kiefe, encoded by JCotsman [1][6]
- **gd1972-04-24.aud.unknown.6956.sbeok.shnf**: source: AUD:RM>C>DAT>CD; SBD:RM>C>DAT>CD [2]. Also: Mixed source: some tracks from audience tape, the rest soundboard, with several tracks being audience [2]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Rheinhalle - April 24, 1972](https://www.dead.net/show/april-24-1972) [16]
